tasks.title: Email about health week activities
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Read this email from your English teacher, Mrs. Hill, and the notes you have made.

promptBlocks.subject: Health week activities
paragraphs: As you know, our school is planning a Health Week next month. We need to choose two main activities for the students. The options are: a healthy cooking workshop, a yoga session in the gym, or a talk by a local doctor about sleep.
Which two activities do you think we should choose? Please give a reason for each choice.
Also, should the activities take place during lesson time or after school? Which do you think is better?
Finally, can you suggest one way to encourage students to sign up?

promptBlocks.heading: Notes for your reply
listItems: Choose two activities and say why you chose each one.
Say if you prefer during lessons or after school – explain why.
Suggest one way to encourage students to sign up.
Ask Mrs. Hill about the budget for the activities.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Mrs. Hill using all the notes.

tasks.title: Article about health week
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: You see this notice on a specialist magazine website.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: Health Week at school – does it really help students?
Do you think a Health Week can make students more interested in healthy living?
What kind of activity do you think is most effective?
Write an article answering these questions and we will put it on our website!

tasks.title: Story about health week
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
"When the programme coordinator handed me the list of health week activities, I noticed something strange at the bottom of the page."
